draft.title: The superannuation guarantee
card: The superannuation guarantee (SG) is a law that requires employers to pay a set share of each worker's ordinary pay into a super fund. The rate is now 12 per cent.
The employer pays this money on top of the wages. It is paid into the worker's super fund, not into their everyday bank account.
Workers can add their own money to super as well. These are called voluntary contributions, and they can build up savings faster.
An employer cannot swap the SG for extra cash in a worker's pay. If an employer does not pay it in full and on time, the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) can make them pay it, plus extra charges.
draft.remember: The law makes employers pay a share of wages into super, and workers can add more.

a.q: Under the superannuation guarantee, what must an employer do for each worker?
opts: Pay a set share of wages into the worker's super fund
Pay the worker a bonus every year into their bank account
Match every dollar the worker adds to their own super
Pay the government a share of each worker's wages as tax
a.why: The guarantee is a law that sends a set share of wages to the worker's super fund. Matching the worker's own extra payments is not required, because those voluntary contributions are the worker's choice.
a.clue: Think about where the employer's payment is sent.

b.q: Priya works at a bakery in Bendigo. She asks her boss to pay her the super share as cash in her next pay instead. What is the best reply?
opts: No, the law says it must go into her super fund
Yes, if she asks, because it is her money to spend
Yes, but only if she is under 25 years old
No, because super is paid only when workers add their own
b.why: The guarantee requires the employer to pay the set share into a super fund, so it cannot be swapped for cash. Priya's own extra payments are optional, but the employer's share does not depend on them.
b.clue: Who decides whether the employer's share is paid, the law or the worker?

a.best: Pay a set share of wages into the worker's super fund

b.best: No, the law says it must go into her super fund

proposal.title: Who contributes to super
card: The superannuation guarantee (SG) is a law that requires employers to pay a set share of most workers' ordinary pay into a super fund. The rate is now 12 per cent.
This money is paid into the worker's super fund, not into their everyday bank account. It is saved for retirement, not spent now.
Workers can add their own money to super as well. These are called voluntary contributions, and they can build up savings faster.
An employer cannot swap the SG for extra cash in a worker's pay. If an employer does not pay it in full and on time, the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) can make them pay it, plus extra charges.
proposal.remember: Employers are required to pay into super. Workers can choose to add more.

a.clue: Think about where the employer's payment is sent.

opts: No, the employer's share must go into her super fund
Yes, if she asks, since the money belongs to her anyway
